ext.setup_intro: Blocking websites needs the buZyist extension in your browser. It's a one-time setup:
ext.open_help: This also copies the extension's folder path and shows the folder in Explorer.
ext._steps: Developer mode, Load unpacked, Select Folder and Reload are Chrome's own labels: use the ones Chrome shows in the language.
ext.step_dev: Turn on Developer mode (the switch at the top right of that page).
ext.step_load:
Drag the selected chrome-extension folder from Explorer onto the page.
Or click Load unpacked, paste the path (Ctrl+V) into the folder picker's address bar, press Enter, then Select Folder.
ext.setup_done_help: The status above turns green within a few seconds of loading the extension.
ext.outdated: buZyist was updated and so was its extension, but your browser is still running the old one ({old}, now {version}). Reload it:
ext.step_reload: Find buZyist Focus and click its Reload icon (the circular arrow). No need to load the folder again.
ext.outdated_help: This message goes away within a few seconds of reloading.
ext.all_set: All set. Keep the extension turned on and buZyist tells it when to block.
ext.copy_failed: Couldn't reach the clipboard; copy the path by hand.
ext.opened_copied: Opened {browser}'s extensions page. The folder path is on your clipboard.
ext.not_found: Couldn't find Chrome. Open chrome://extensions in your browser.
ext.not_found_copied: Couldn't find Chrome. Open chrome://extensions in your browser. The folder path is on your clipboard.

limits.site_help: These work all day, with or without a session running. A site is blocked once any of its time limits is used up, or during its blocked hours. Time counts while the site is the active tab in a browser window you're using. Needs the browser extension (Websites tab); reload it after updating buZyist.
limits.app_help: The same limits for Windows apps, measured by buZyist: time counts while the app's window is in front and you're using the PC. Once a limit is reached, buZyist closes the app; pick Beep to keep it open and just hear how long it's been in front (again every few minutes it stays there; you pick how often). App limits stay on this PC.

budget._: A time limit: {minutes} min in each period of {n} units.

limits.app_beeps: Beeps when reached, again every {n} min; the app stays open

editor.sites_help: Several websites can share one limit: the time adds up across all of them.
editor.apps_help: Program names, as Task Manager's Details tab shows them, separated by commas; the ones running now are suggested as you type. Several apps can share one limit: the time adds up across all of them.
editor.hours_help: Hours ending before they start run past midnight (22:00 to 06:00). 00:00 to 00:00 is the whole day.

sync.limits_help: Through Chrome sync: on each PC, sign one Chrome profile in to the same Google account, with sync on, and load the buZyist extension there. Time on Instagram here then counts on your other PCs too. Only the limits are shared; your other settings stay on each PC.

sync.session_help: Another PC on the same BUSY Bar then shows the task you started here, instead of "Started on the bar". Turn it on on both PCs.
sync.owner_help: Pick the profile signed in to the account you use on your other PCs. Other profiles on this PC still enforce the limits and count time; they just don't share it.
